findings.issue: Five of the model's features are weather measured on the day being predicted: temp, atemp, hum and windspeed (listed as RAW_FEATURE_COLS in src/config.py:59), plus weather_severity. The comment says these are 'available to a forecaster', but nothing in the code supports that: a daily weather value is only known by the end of that day, the same time as cnt. I refit the same ridge pipeline without these five columns. It scored valid R^2 0.4668 and test R^2 0.4516, against persistence at 0.4507 and 0.5099.
findings.why_it_matters: This is not target leakage: check_identity finds no restatement of cnt. But the persistence baseline only uses data up to yesterday, while the models also see today's actual weather. On test, the whole margin ridge has over persistence (0.6124 vs 0.5099) comes from these same-day columns. The report should either describe this as a nowcast that assumes perfect weather, or use forecast or lagged weather, before claiming the model beats persistence as a forecast.

findings.issue: The --target-transform path only fits ridge and hgb. All five committed reports/target_*.json files contain model scores with no mean, persistence or anchor-only baseline. That includes target_diff_cnt_roll_7_test.json, the only file with the Exercise 4 test score (hgb 0.6282). I computed the right comparison for an anchor-difference model, which is the anchor alone: valid 0.5945 and test 0.4796. The valid number appears only in DECISIONS.md; the test number appears nowhere.
findings.why_it_matters: The rule is a baseline next to every model score. reports/metrics.json meets it with both baselines. The transform outputs don't, so hgb's 0.6282 on test can't be compared to persistence (0.5099) or the anchor (0.4796) from the file that holds it.

findings.issue: fit_and_score scores the test split by default (splits=("valid", "test")), so every `make train` / `make all` computes, prints and writes test scores. Commit 8653a30, which adopted weather_severity_lag_1, committed new test numbers in the same change (ridge test 0.5833 -> 0.6124; hgb -0.4975 -> -0.4687).
findings.why_it_matters: DECISIONS.md:9 says the test set was 'touched once, after all feature work'. The pipeline makes that impossible: test scores were produced and committed during feature selection. Saying 'test numbers not consulted' is a statement about behaviour, and the code doesn't enforce it. Test scoring should be opt-in, as it already is for the transform runs (--test).

findings.issue: test_beats_the_mean_baseline refits ridge and asserts its R^2 on the test split is above 0.4. It runs on every `make test`, and the new-feature skill runs `make test` after every feature change. It never compares against the mean baseline its name refers to (that baseline scores -2.14 on test). The 0.4 threshold is also below persistence (0.5099), so a model worse than 'yesterday again' passes.
findings.why_it_matters: This makes the held-out test set a pass/fail gate in the development loop, which is a form of tuning on test, and the check is too weak to catch a model that loses to the baseline that matters. It should run on validation and compare against baseline_persistence's score.

findings.issue: CLAUDE.md:11 says `make all` 'reproduces every number in REPORT.md', and README.md:48 says to record the model used in REPORT.md. No REPORT.md exists in the working tree or in git history.
findings.why_it_matters: The documented reproduction target is missing, so it can't be checked whether the write-up's numbers (and whether it puts baselines next to scores) match the pipeline. What I could check reproduces exactly: in a clean copy of HEAD, `make all` regenerated reports/metrics.json byte for byte, a second run gave the same result, all five target_*.json files matched, all 19 tests passed, and HGB uses random_state=0.

findings.issue: The docs no longer match the code. DECISIONS.md:6 cites 'honest ridge 0.583', which was the test R^2 before weather_severity_lag_1; the current pipeline gives 0.6124 on test and 0.667 on valid. README.md:25 says `make test` runs 14 tests; it runs 19.
findings.why_it_matters: These are numbers presented as results that the documented command no longer produces. A reader checking them against `make all` will find mismatches.
